literature.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期狂犬病病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 研究发现,2000 年至 2024 年间,美国只有约 7% 的人类 狂犬病 死亡得到证实,估计有 856 人(95% CI:213-2220)人死于未确诊的 狂犬病。这相当于每年平均有 34.2 人死亡(95% CI:8.5–88.8)。 [10.1038/s44528-026-00031-4]
GenBank 中存放的哈萨克斯坦 狂犬病病毒 分离株显示,无论 宿主 属于何种物种,它们都属于世界谱系并形成单一系统发育簇。 [10.3390/pathogens15090886]
亲属报告的主要情绪反应包括悲伤(18/37)、无助(15/37)、愤怒(8/37)、震惊(9/37)、被遗弃感(1/37)和内疚(7/37)。死亡后,侵入性记忆、睡眠障碍(24/37)、噩梦(15/37)和回避动物(11/37)几乎普遍报道,表明创伤后心理困扰和长期悲伤。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10796782/v1]
结果表明,在不同的细胞系中,牛 β-珠蛋白 5'UTR 对报告蛋白的翻译更高。牛β-珠蛋白5'UTR不仅提高了报告蛋白的翻译效率,而且支持不同抗原蛋白的表达。 [10.1007/s10529-026-03778-6]
狂犬病 在社区中的总体认知度较高,为 92.1%,其中肯尼亚基图伊农村地区居民的认知度显著高于内罗毕城市居民(98.4% vs 84.8%;p < 0.05)。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10582245/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The study found that only around 7% of human rabies deaths in the US were confirmed between 2000 and 2024, with an estimated 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) deaths due to undiagnosed rabies. This corresponds to an average of 34.2 (95% CI: 8.5–88.8) deaths per year. [10.1038/s44528-026-00031-4]

Kazakhstani rabies virus isolates deposited in GenBank revealed that all belong to a cosmopolitan lineage and form a single phylogenetic cluster, regardless of host species. [10.3390/pathogens15090886]

Relatives reported predominant emotional responses including sadness (18/37), helplessness (15/37), anger (8/37), shock (9/37), feelings of abandonment (1/37), and guilt (7/37). [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10796782/v1]

The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5'UTR in different cell lines. Bovine β-globin 5'UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. [10.1007/s10529-026-03778-6]

The delay rate was 29.7%. Eight independent factors were identified. Adults had a 34% higher risk of delay than children (aOR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.22-1.47, P < 0.001). Grade III exposure was associated with more prompt care-seeking (aOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.65-0.73, P < 0.001). [10.3389/fpubh.2026.1911137]

papers.title: Molecular Genetic Analysis of the Rabies Virus in Wild and Domestic Animals of Kazakhstan and the Development of a Diagnostic System
papers.abstract: Rabies remains one of the most significant zoonotic infections, characterized by high mortality. In Kazakhstan, the virus circulates among both domestic and wild animals, necessitating ongoing molecular genetic monitoring and improved laboratory diagnostic methods. The aim of this study was to investigate the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating among animals in Kazakhstan using nucleoprotein (N) gene analysis and to develop a regionally adapted real-time RT-PCR method for its detection. Kazakhstani rabies virus isolates deposited in GenBank revealed that all belong to a cosmopolitan lineage and form a single phylogenetic cluster, regardless of host species. Isolates from neighboring countries, including China and Russia, were also included in this cluster, demonstrating the regional relationship of circulating virus variants. The obtained data were used to develop a real-time PCR method based on the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating in Kazakhstan. The diagnostic performance of the method was evaluated using 144 samples of various origins obtained from domestic and wild animals, including bats. The developed assay demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.4%, a specificity of 98.4%, and a diagnostic efficiency of 96.5%. The proposed method ensures reliable detection of rabies virus variants circulating in Kazakhstan and can be used for laboratory diagnostics and epidemiological monitoring.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating among animals in Kazakhstan and develop a regionally adapted real-time RT-PCR method for its detection. The research found that all Kazakhstani rabies virus isolates belong to a cosmopolitan lineage and form a single phylogenetic cluster, regardless of host species. The study included isolates from neighboring countries, such as China and Russia, to demonstrate the regional relationship of circulating virus variants. The developed assay demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.4%, a specificity of 98.4%, and a diagnostic efficiency of 96.5%. The method was evaluated using 144 samples from domestic and wild animals, including bats, and was found to be reliable for detecting rabies virus variants in Kazakhstan. The findings have significant implications for improving laboratory diagnostics and epidemiological monitoring of rabies in the region. The study's evidence is strong, but its generalizability may be limited to the specific geographic and host contexts examined.

papers.title_zh: 哈萨克斯坦野生动物与家畜中狂犬病病毒的分子遗传分析及诊断系统开发
papers.source_body_en: Rabies remains one of the most significant zoonotic infections, characterized by high mortality. In Kazakhstan, the virus circulates among both domestic and wild animals, necessitating ongoing molecular genetic monitoring and improved laboratory diagnostic methods. The aim of this study was to investigate the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating among animals in Kazakhstan using nucleoprotein (N) gene analysis and to develop a regionally adapted real-time RT-PCR method for its detection. Kazakhstani rabies virus isolates deposited in GenBank revealed that all belong to a cosmopolitan lineage and form a single phylogenetic cluster, regardless of host species. Isolates from neighboring countries, including China and Russia, were also included in this cluster, demonstrating the regional relationship of circulating virus variants. The obtained data were used to develop a real-time PCR method based on the genetic characteristics of the rabies virus circulating in Kazakhstan. The diagnostic performance of the method was evaluated using 144 samples of various origins obtained from domestic and wild animals, including bats. The developed assay demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.4%, a specificity of 98.4%, and a diagnostic efficiency of 96.5%. The proposed method ensures reliable detection of rabies virus variants circulating in Kazakhstan and can be used for laboratory diagnostics and epidemiological monitoring.

papers.title: Atypical neuroimaging in rabies encephalitis: A case report of concurrent cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in a nine-year-old patient
papers.abstract: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient's condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human rabies is a uniformly fatal encephalitis that poses diagnostic challenges when exposure history is absent, creating uncertainty in early clinical recognition and management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-patient case report describes a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation, and hydrophobia without a reported animal exposure history.
analysis.methods: Diagnostic evaluation included brain MRI to identify encephalitic changes and a nuchal skin biopsy analyzed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction for rabies virus RNA confirmation.
analysis.main_results: MRI revealed bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes consistent with rabies encephalitis and an atypical finding of extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis involving the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the MRI as demonstrating the dual diagnostic role of imaging in rabies—supporting early etiological diagnosis while simultaneously identifying a rare macrovascular complication, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the importance of MRI in acute encephalitis for both etiological diagnosis of rabies and detection of concurrent macrovascular complications that may influence management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single case report with no control group, restricting generalizability and precluding causal inference; the strength of evidence is low.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with clinical features of rabies encephalitis despite no reported animal exposure. Brain MRI showed classic bilateral thalamic and temporal lobe hyperintensities suggestive of rabies and an atypical finding of right transverse and sigmoid sinus thrombosis. Rabies virus RNA was confirmed by RT-PCR from a nuchal skin biopsy. Despite intensive care and anticoagulation, the patient died on day 9. The authors emphasize MRI’s dual diagnostic utility in rabies—identifying encephalitic changes and concurrent macrovascular complications—but the single-case design limits broader conclusions.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Human rabies is a uniformly fatal encephalitis that poses diagnostic challenges when exposure history is absent, creating uncertainty in early clinical recognition and management.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This single-patient case report describes a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation, and hydrophobia without a reported animal exposure history.
analysis_en.methods: Diagnostic evaluation included brain MRI to identify encephalitic changes and a nuchal skin biopsy analyzed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction for rabies virus RNA confirmation.
analysis_en.main_results: MRI revealed bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes consistent with rabies encephalitis and an atypical finding of extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis involving the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the MRI as demonstrating the dual diagnostic role of imaging in rabies—supporting early etiological diagnosis while simultaneously identifying a rare macrovascular complication, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case highlights the importance of MRI in acute encephalitis for both etiological diagnosis of rabies and detection of concurrent macrovascular complications that may influence management.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single case report with no control group, restricting generalizability and precluding causal inference; the strength of evidence is low.

papers.title_zh: 狂犬病 脑炎的非典型神经影像:一名 9 岁患者并发脑静脉窦血栓形成的 病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Human rabies is a fatal viral encephalitis that presents a profound diagnostic challenge in the absence of a known history of animal exposure. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy from Morocco who presented with fever, seizures, psychomotor agitation, hypersalivation and hydrophobia, despite no reported history of an animal bite or scratch. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) served as a critical diagnostic tool, strongly suggesting rabies encephalitis by revealing classic bilateral symmetric grey matter hyperintensities in the thalami and temporal lobes. Concurrently, MRI revealed an atypical and rare macrovascular finding: extensive cerebral venous sinus thrombosis of the right transverse and sigmoid sinuses, which likely accounted for additional asymmetric white matter changes. A nuchal skin biopsy analyzed via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction confirmed the presence of rabies virus RNA. Despite aggressive neurocritical care and therapeutic anticoagulation, the patient's condition deteriorated, and he passed away on day 9 of admission. This case underscores the dual role of MRI in acute encephalitis: guiding early etiological diagnosis of rabies and identifying concurrent, clinically significant macrovascular complications like cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

papers.title: Psychological effects of rabies on the relatives of people who died from human rabies in Côte d'Ivoire between 2023 and 2025: Qualitative Observational Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background : the psychological impact of rabies on the relatives of people who died from the disease remains largely unexplored. The aim of this study was to analyse the psychological effects of rabies on the relatives of people who died from human rabies in Côte d’Ivoire. Patients and methods : A single-center descriptive study was conducted from January to June 2026 using a qualitative approach, enabled an in-depth exploration of the experiences of these relatives. The participants, aged at least 18 years, were relatives of people who died from confirmed or suspected human rabies between 2023 and 2025, identified from the death notification register of the Anti-Rabies Center of the National Institute of Public Hygiene. The data were collected by individual semi-structured interviews conducted until data saturation was achieved, then subjected to a thematic analysis. Faced with the announcement of the diagnosis and its fatal prognosis, sadness (18/37), helplessness (15/37), anger (8/37) and shock (9/37), feelings of abandonment (1/37) and guilt (7/37) were the predominant emotional responses. After death, relatives reported almost universal intrusive memories, sleep disturbances (24/37), nightmares (15/37) and avoidance of animals (11/37), suggestive of post-traumatic psychological distress and prolonged grief, aggravated by the disruption of traditional funeral practices. Coping relied almost exclusively on prayer (28/37), and family and community support (18/37), with no participant reporting receipt of any formal psychological support. Conclusion : The burden of rabies extends beyond mortality and includes profound and lasting psychological suffering among the relatives of people who die from human rabies. The integration of a culturally appropriate psychosocial component into rabies management would help relieve families and strengthen awareness towards achieving the goal of eliminating rabies by 2030.

papers.abstract_original: Abstract Background : the psychological impact of rabies on the relatives of people who died from the disease remains largely unexplored. The aim of this study was to analyse the psychological effects of rabies on the relatives of people who died from human rabies in Côte d’Ivoire. Patients and methods : A single-center descriptive study was conducted from January to June 2026 using a qualitative approach, enabled an in-depth exploration of the experiences of these relatives. The participants, aged at least 18 years, were relatives of people who died from confirmed or suspected human rabies between 2023 and 2025, identified from the death notification register of the Anti-Rabies Center of the National Institute of Public Hygiene. The data were collected by individual semi-structured interviews conducted until data saturation was achieved, then subjected to a thematic analysis. Faced with the announcement of the diagnosis and its fatal prognosis, sadness (18/37), helplessness (15/37), anger (8/37) and shock (9/37), feelings of abandonment (1/37) and guilt (7/37) were the predominant emotional responses. After death, relatives reported almost universal intrusive memories, sleep disturbances (24/37), nightmares (15/37) and avoidance of animals (11/37), suggestive of post-traumatic psychological distress and prolonged grief, aggravated by the disruption of traditional funeral practices. Coping relied almost exclusively on prayer (28/37), and family and community support (18/37), with no participant reporting receipt of any formal psychological support. Conclusion : The burden of rabies extends beyond mortality and includes profound and lasting psychological suffering among the relatives of people who die from human rabies. The integration of a culturally appropriate psychosocial component into rabies management would help relieve families and strengthen awareness towards achieving the goal of eliminating rabies by 2030.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative observational study in Côte d'Ivoire examined the psychological effects on relatives of people who died from human rabies between 2023 and 2025. Using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis, the research identified predominant emotional responses such as sadness, helplessness, anger, and shock, alongside post-traumatic symptoms including intrusive memories, sleep disturbances, nightmares, and avoidance behaviors. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:狂犬病 对死于该疾病的人的亲属的心理影响在很大程度上仍有待探索。本研究的目的是分析 狂犬病 对科特迪瓦人类 狂犬病 死亡者亲属的心理影响。患者和方法:从 2026 年 1 月至 6 月进行了一项单中心描述性研究,采用定性方法,深入探讨了这些亲属的经历。这些参与者年龄至少 18 岁,是 2023 年至 2025 年间死于确诊或疑似人类 狂犬病 的人的亲属,这些人是从国家公共卫生研究所抗 狂犬病 中心的死亡通知登记册中确定的。通过单独的半结构化访谈收集数据,直至达到数据饱和,然后进行主题分析。面对诊断的宣布及其致命的预后,悲伤(18/37)、无助(15/37)、愤怒(8/37)和震惊(9/37)、被遗弃感(1/37)和内疚(7/37)是主要的情绪反应。死后,亲属报告了几乎普遍的侵入性记忆、睡眠障碍(24/37)、噩梦(15/37)和回避动物(11/37),这表明创伤后心理困扰和长期悲伤,而传统丧葬习俗的破坏加剧了这种情况。应对几乎完全依赖祈祷(28/37)以及家庭和社区支持(18/37),没有参与者报告收到任何正式的心理支持。结论:狂犬病 的负担超出了 死亡率 的范畴,还包括死于人类 狂犬病 的人的亲属所承受的深刻而持久的心理痛苦。将文化上适当的社会心理成分纳入 狂犬病 管理将有助于缓解家庭压力,并增强意识,以实现到 2030 年消除 狂犬病 的目标。

papers.full_text: Based on multiple instances of human-to-human rabies transmission via organ or tissue transplantation from initially undiagnosed rabies-infected donors, we estimate 856 (213–2220) human rabies deaths in the United States (US) from 2000 to 2024, meaning that only around 7% of human rabies deaths in the US were confirmed during this period. Subjects Article PDF In February 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) of the United States (US) diagnosed rabies in a kidney transplant recipient and subsequently in the donor who died in December 20241. This event marks the fourth transplant-related rabies transmission from an initially undiagnosed donor in the US since 1978, following transmission events identified from the three earlier donors—who died in 19782, 20043, and 20114—which resulted in six deaths, in one cornea recipient, three kidney recipients, one liver recipient and one arterial-segment recipient. In each case transplantation was allowed because rabies had not been diagnosed in the deceased donor before organ or tissue transplantation. Additional transplant recipients from these donors remained asymptomatic following post-exposure prophylaxis1,4. Each year, very few rabies cases have been confirmed in the US, including Puerto Rico, on average 2.4 per annum from 2000 to 2024 (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Data)5. However, the instances of rabies transmission from initially undiagnosed deceased donors suggest that many human deaths due to rabies are not diagnosed as such, considering that only a small percentage of people dying in the US become organ and tissue donors. An estimate of the number of human deaths in the US due to undiagnosed rabies in the 25 years from 2000 to 2024 can be obtained from the identified number of deceased donors who died of rabies undiagnosed prior to transplantation1,3,4 (n = 3) divided by the number of deceased donors (n = 239,251, Fig. 1) and multiplied by the number of deaths (n = 68,266,224, Fig. 1) (see Supplementary Data for data sources and estimation). The underlying assumption is that donors have experienced the average national risk of rabies infection. This gives an estimate of 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) undiagnosed human rabies deaths over the 25-year period in the US, corresponding to an average of 34.2 (95% CI: 8.5–88.8) deaths per annum. Our central estimate suggests that only around 7% (i.e. 0.07 = 2.4/36.6 deaths per annum) of human rabies cases in the general population were confirmed in recent years, and even its confidence limits indicate that, in the best-case scenario, only around 22% were diagnosed. In order to argue that the reported number of rabies cases is consistent with complete surveillance, deceased donors would need to have a rabies risk approximately 14 times that of decedents in the general population. Both the risk of rabies infection and the probability of becoming a donor after death might be associated with geographical, occupational, and socioeconomic factors. Therefore, data on predictors of rabies infection and donation after death would help refine our estimate. While canine rabies is notoriously under-detected in affected countries6, our estimate highlights that under-detection of human cases could also occur in countries in which rabies risk is limited mostly to wildlife exposure. The long and variable incubation period, ranging weeks to one year7, likely contributes to under-detection in the US. Additionally, a substantial number of exposures may go either unobserved (e.g. non-apparent injuries) or unrecognised as posing a rabies risk (e.g. superficial scratches or a general lack of risk awareness in the region of residence or travel)8. Consequently, substantial under-detection in the general population may both result from and contribute to an underappreciation of rabies transmission, thereby sustaining ongoing transmission risks to transplant recipients. Although these factors would also contribute to under-detection in canine-rabies-endemic countries, their exact mechanisms and relative contributions likely differ from those in the US, given differing diagnostic capacities and rabies risk profiles (i.e. exposure to wildlife versus free-roaming or owned dogs). Our results highlight the need to enhance rabies diagnosis, for example, by increasing risk awareness in the public, obtaining in-depth exposure histories, considering potential geographical, occupational, and socioeconomic risk factors independently of exposure histories, and explicitly including rabies among the differential diagnoses for patients who die from unexplained clinical signs compatible with rabies, including encephalitis. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the under-detection of human rabies cases in the United States, highlighting the risk of undiagnosed rabies infections in deceased donors leading to transmission via organ or tissue transplantation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed rabies transmission events from 2000 to 2024, focusing on cases where rabies was transmitted through organ or tissue transplantation from donors who were not diagnosed with rabies before death. It included data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and other sources.
analysis.methods: The researchers estimated the number of undiagnosed rabies deaths by dividing the number of identified rabies-related donor deaths by the total number of deceased donors and multiplying by the total number of deaths in the US. They assumed that donors had the average national risk of rabies infection.
analysis.main_results: The study found that only around 7% of human rabies deaths in the US were confirmed between 2000 and 2024, with an estimated 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) deaths due to undiagnosed rabies. This corresponds to an average of 34.2 (95% CI: 8.5–88.8) deaths per year.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of substantial under-detection of rabies cases in the US, emphasizing that the current surveillance system may not capture the true burden of the disease due to the low rate of rabies diagnosis in deceased donors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that the existing surveillance system for rabies in the US significantly underestimates the number of human rabies deaths, which has important implications for improving diagnostic practices and donor screening protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on the assumption that donors have the average national risk of rabies infection, which may not account for geographical, occupational, or socioeconomic variations. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on reported cases and extrapolation.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the under-detection of human rabies cases in the United States, estimating that 856 (95% CI: 213–2220) deaths occurred due to undiagnosed rabies infections in deceased donors between 2000 and 2024. Only around 7% of these deaths were confirmed, indicating a significant gap in surveillance. The study analyzed rabies transmission events through organ or tissue transplantation, noting that four such cases have been identified since 1978. The authors suggest that the current diagnostic system fails to capture the true burden of rabies, as only a small percentage of deaths lead to organ donation. The findings emphasize the need for improved donor screening and diagnostic practices to prevent future transmission. However, the study's estimate is based on assumptions about donor risk and may not account for all variables, limiting its strength.

elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过将已确定的与 狂犬病 相关的捐献者死亡人数除以已故捐献者总数,再乘以美国的死亡总数来估计未确诊的 狂犬病 死亡人数。他们假设捐赠者感染 狂犬病 的风险与全国平均水平相同。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为美国 狂犬病 病例严重检测不足的证据,并强调由于已故捐赠者中 狂犬病 诊断 的发生率较低,当前的 狂犬病 系统可能无法捕获该疾病的真正负担。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,美国现有的 狂犬病 系统明显低估了人类 狂犬病 死亡人数,这对于改进诊断实践和捐赠者筛查方案具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于这样的假设:捐赠者感染 狂犬病 的全国平均风险是相同的,这可能无法解释地理、职业或社会经济差异。证据是中等的,因为它是基于报告的案例和推断。

papers.title: 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) of bovine β-globin in the mRNA constructs translates different types of antigenic proteins.
papers.abstract: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5'UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5'UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5'UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5'UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5'UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5'UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5'UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of the bovine β-globin 5'UTR as a universal enhancer for mRNA translation efficiency in vaccine development. The research aimed to address the challenge of using natural 5'UTRs, which are gene-specific, by evaluating synthetic mRNA constructs with different 5'UTRs. The authors cloned six natural 5'UTRs from various sources and assessed their impact on translation efficiency using in vitro methods. The results showed that the bovine β-globin 5'UTR significantly enhanced the translation of reporter proteins and supported the expression of different antigenic proteins, including rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG). The study suggests that this 5'UTR could be a valuable component in mRNA vaccine designs targeting rabies virus and related diseases. However, the findings are based on in vitro experiments and lack in vivo validation, which limits their applicability to real-world scenarios. The evidence is moderate, as it does not include clinical or epidemiological data.

papers.title: Temporal trends and determinants of delayed care-seeking after rabies exposure: a 27,930-patient analysis in Tianjin
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Prompt care-seeking after rabies exposure is essential for effective post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). This study aimed to identify independent factors associated with care-seeking delay and to map the full PEP pathway. METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 27,930 patients attending the rabies PEP clinic at Santan Hospital, Tianjin, between February 2022 and January 2026. Delay was defined as >12 h from exposure to registration. Multivariable logistic regression, combined with XGBoost and SHAP, identified independent factors for delay and quantified their relative importance. Restricted cubic splines examined the non-linear relationship between age and delay. Subgroup analysis assessed the stability of the association of grade III exposure with more prompt care-seeking. A Sankey diagram traced the PEP pathway. RESULTS: The delay rate was 29.7%. Eight independent factors were identified. Adults had a 34% higher risk of delay than children (aOR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.22-1.47, P < 0.001). Grade III exposure was associated with more prompt care-seeking (aOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.65-0.73, P < 0.001). Previous rabies vaccination (aOR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.11-1.23, P < 0.001) and inadequate wound management (aOR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.31-1.88, P < 0.001) were associated with higher delay risk. Age showed a non-linear relationship with delay risk, with adults at highest risk. The Sankey diagram showed that inadequate wound management was rare in the PEP pathway, and the two-dose booster schedule achieved a much higher completion rate than the standard schedule. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that adults may face the highest risk of care-seeking delay, and that improving healthcare access for adults and promoting simplified vaccination schedules may be key to improving PEP quality.

papers.title: Rabies in Military Personnel: Epidemiology, Clinical Challenges, and Strategies for Prevention and Management
papers.abstract: For deployed military personnel, a single exposure from a rabies-infected animal can become a death sentence. With a case fatality rate approaching 100%, rabies remains a serious, yet insufficiently acknowledged hazard for service members, for whom prevention in operational environments poses unique challenges. We conducted a systematic literature search to identify relevant studies on rabies risk in armed forces personnel. By analysing rabies-related fatalities in the military, this review highlights the operational challenges posed by animal bites during deployment, including underreporting and delayed access to care, which compromise timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration. Special emphasis is placed on prevention strategies, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and animal control protocols tailored to military settings. Its aim is to provide a comprehensive, evidence-based resource for healthcare professionals involved in the protection of deployed forces against this ancient yet still deadly infectious disease.

The central question is the epidemiology, clinical challenges, and prevention strategies for rabies in deployed forces, with an emphasis on the risks posed by animal bites and the challenges of timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic literature search to identify relevant studies on rabies risk in armed forces personnel. The methodology involved analyzing rabies-related fatalities in the military to highlight operational challenges, including underreporting and delayed access to care.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that rabies remains a serious, yet insufficiently acknowledged hazard for military personnel, with a case fatality rate approaching 100%. It emphasizes the critical need for prevention strategies, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and animal control protocols tailored to military settings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is heterogeneity in the evidence regarding the effectiveness of prevention strategies in operational environments. The review notes that underreporting and delayed access to care compromise timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration, creating evidence gaps in understanding the full scope of rabies risk for deployed forces.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for improved surveillance, better access to care, and the development of prevention strategies specifically adapted to military contexts. It also underscores the importance of education and training for military personnel to recognize and respond to rabies exposure effectively.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines rabies virus and rabies disease in military personnel, focusing on the epidemiology, clinical challenges, and prevention strategies. It highlights the high case fatality rate of rabies and the unique operational challenges faced by deployed forces, including underreporting and delayed access to post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). The review emphasizes the importance of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and tailored animal control protocols. It also identifies evidence gaps related to the effectiveness of prevention strategies and the need for improved surveillance and education in military settings.

papers.title_zh: 军事人员中的狂犬病:临床挑战、预防与管理策略
papers.source_body_en: For deployed military personnel, a single exposure from a rabies-infected animal can become a death sentence. With a case fatality rate approaching 100%, rabies remains a serious, yet insufficiently acknowledged hazard for service members, for whom prevention in operational environments poses unique challenges. We conducted a systematic literature search to identify relevant studies on rabies risk in armed forces personnel. By analysing rabies-related fatalities in the military, this review highlights the operational challenges posed by animal bites during deployment, including underreporting and delayed access to care, which compromise timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration. Special emphasis is placed on prevention strategies, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and animal control protocols tailored to military settings. Its aim is to provide a comprehensive, evidence-based resource for healthcare professionals involved in the protection of deployed forces against this ancient yet still deadly infectious disease.

papers.title: Zoonotic disease risk perceptions associated with commercial wildlife activities in Southeast Asia: A scoping review
papers.abstract: Abstract Background : Zoonotic disease emergence is closely linked to human-wildlife interactions, particularly in commercial wildlife activities where livelihoods, conservation, and health intersect. In Southeast Asia, wildlife hunting, trade, and farming remain integral to many communities, yet limited evidence has been synthesized on how communities engaged in these activities perceive associated zoonotic disease risks. This scoping review examines community perceptions of zoonotic disease risks associated with commercial wildlife activities and explores their implications for One Health research and practice. Methods : Peer-reviewed studies published in English between 2000 and 2024 were identified through PubMed and Google Scholar. Eligible studies examining community perceptions of health or zoonotic disease risks associated with wildlife hunting, trade, farming, or consumption in Southeast Asia were included in the review. Data were extracted and analyzed thematically to identify patterns, knowledge gaps, and implications for research and practice. Results : Eight studies from Thailand, Indonesia, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, and Myanmar met the inclusion criteria. Studies used qualitative or mixed-methods approaches involving hunters, traders, farmers, consumers, and communities with wildlife contact. Study findings showed partial awareness of zoonotic risks among study populations, often limited to diseases such as avian influenza and rabies. Gaps in translating awareness into preventive practices were highlighted, driven by livelihood dependence, poverty, limited access to services and facilities, and broader structural constraints. Cultural beliefs, gender, and education also shaped risk perceptions and responses, and illegal or informal trade contexts complicated engagement and data collection. Conclusions : Community perceptions of zoonotic disease risk in Southeast Asia are shaped by intersecting social, economic, cultural, and livelihood factors. Effective strategies to reduce zoonotic disease risk associated with commercial wildlife activities require cross-sectoral, context-sensitive approaches that integrate community perspectives into communication and services across the conservation, public health, agriculture, and veterinary sectors. Risk reduction strategies should also move beyond awareness raising to address structural barriers that limit communities’ access to relevant information and services, thereby supporting more equitable and sustainable zoonotic disease prevention in Southeast Asia. One Health impact statement This scoping review highlights the importance of understanding how communities engaged in commercial wildlife activities perceive zoonotic disease risks at the human-animal-environment interfaces in Southeast Asia. By synthesizing limited evidence across health, social, and ecological dimensions, the review demonstrates that awareness of zoonotic disease risks alone is often insufficient to support preventive practices when livelihood dependence, limited access to services, sociocultural beliefs, and broader structural barriers shape decision-making and behaviors. The findings underscore the importance of integrating community perspectives into One Health research and implementation through context-sensitive, cross-sectoral approaches involving conservation, public health, agriculture, and veterinary sectors. While community perceptions alone do not constitute transdisciplinary One Health practice, understanding local experiences, priorities, and constraints provides a critical foundation for coproducing more equitable, culturally grounded, and sustainable zoonotic disease prevention strategies.

source_records.abstract: Background : Zoonotic disease emergence is closely linked to human-wildlife interactions, particularly in commercial wildlife activities where livelihoods, conservation, and health intersect. In Southeast Asia, wildlife hunting, trade, and farming remain integral to many communities, yet limited evidence has been synthesized on how communities engaged in these activities perceive associated zoonotic disease risks. Methods : Peer-reviewed studies published in English between 2000 and 2024 were identified through PubMed and Google Scholar. Studies used qualitative or mixed-methods approaches involving hunters, traders, farmers, consumers, and communities with wildlife contact. papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景:人畜共患疾病的出现与人类与野生动物的相互作用密切相关,特别是在生计、保护和健康交叉的商业野生动物活动中。在东南亚,野生动物狩猎、贸易和农业仍然是许多社区不可或缺的一部分,但关于从事这些活动的社区如何看待相关的人畜共患疾病风险,综合证据有限。本范围审查考察了社区对与商业野生动物活动相关的人畜共患疾病风险的看法,并探讨了它们对 One Health 研究和实践的影响。方法:通过 PubMed 和 Google Scholar 识别 2000 年至 2024 年间以英文发表的同行评审研究。审查中纳入了符合条件的研究,该研究考察了社区对东南亚野生动物狩猎、贸易、农业或消费相关的健康或人畜共患疾病风险的看法。数据被提取并按主题进行分析,以确定模式、知识差距以及对研究和实践的影响。结果:来自泰国、印度尼西亚、老挝人民民主共和国和缅甸的八项研究符合纳入标准。研究采用定性或混合方法,涉及猎人、贸易商、农民、消费者和与野生动物接触的社区。研究结果显示,研究人群对人畜共患风险的认识有限,通常仅限于禽流感和 狂犬病 等疾病。由于生计依赖、贫困、获得服务和设施的机会有限以及更广泛的结构性限制,在将认识转化为预防实践方面存在着差距。文化信仰、性别和教育也影响了风险认知和应对措施,非法或非正式贸易环境使参与和数据收集变得复杂。结论:东南亚社区对人畜共患疾病风险的看法是由社会、经济、文化和生计等交叉因素决定的。减少与野生动物商业活动相关的人畜共患疾病风险的有效策略需要采取跨部门、因地制宜的方法,将社区观点纳入保护、公共卫生、农业和兽医部门的沟通和服务中。降低风险战略还应超越提高认识的范围,解决限制社区获取相关信息和服务的结构性障碍,从而支持东南亚更加公平和可持续的人畜共患疾病预防。一份健康影响声明 这项范围界定审查强调了了解从事商业野生动物活动的社区如何看待东南亚人类与动物环境界面上的人畜共患疾病风险的重要性。通过综合健康、社会和生态方面的有限证据,该审查表明,当生计依赖、获得服务的机会有限、社会文化信仰和更广泛的结构性障碍影响决策和行为时,仅对人畜共患疾病风险的认识往往不足以支持预防措施。研究结果强调了通过涉及保护、公共卫生、农业和兽医部门的具体情况敏感的跨部门方法将社区观点纳入同一个健康研究和实施的重要性。虽然社区认知本身并不能构成跨学科的“同一个健康”实践,但了解当地经验、优先事项和限制因素为共同制定更公平、有文化基础和可持续的人畜共患疾病预防策略提供了重要基础。

papers.title: Passive Immunization Hesitancy Among Rabies-Exposed Individuals in China: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Rabies is an almost universally fatal disease for which post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), including passive immunization (PI) with rabies immunoglobulin or monoclonal antibodies, remains the only effective intervention. Despite established clinical guidelines, real-world PI utilization remains suboptimal. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and determinants of PI hesitancy among previously unvaccinated patients with Category III rabies exposure in China. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional questionnaire study was conducted at 12 rabies PEP clinics or emergency departments in 12 provinces of mainland China. The analysis included 585 previously unvaccinated adults with Category III rabies exposure who initially hesitated to receive or declined PI. The questionnaire collected sociodemographic characteristics, exposure profiles, awareness of the early protection gap, reasons for initial PI hesitancy or refusal, the decision to receive PI during the same clinical encounter, and PI product selection. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with PI treatment decisions, with results reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs); reason-specific models used the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction. All inferential analyses were restricted to adults. Results: Among 5068 eligible previously unvaccinated patients with Category III rabies exposure, 2866 (57%) initially hesitated to receive or declined recommended PI. Of 617 questionnaire respondents, 32 minors were excluded, leaving 585 adults for all inferential analyses. The leading reasons for initial hesitancy were lack of understanding of the immediate protective role of PI (199/585, 34%), belief that vaccination alone was sufficient (194/585, 33%), and high cost (178/585, 30%). During the same clinical encounter, 320/585 adults (55%) chose to receive PI. Awareness of the early protection gap (aOR 2.63, 95% CI 1.75–3.98, p < 0.001) and bachelor’s degree or higher (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.07–2.43, p = 0.023) were positively associated with the decision to receive PI, whereas head/face wounds were negatively associated (aOR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30–0.92, p = 0.026). In reason-specific models, lack of knowledge about immediate protection was associated with higher odds of choosing PI (aOR 2.43, 95% CI 1.62–3.68, BH-FDR p < 0.001), whereas high cost was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.27–0.62, BH-FDR p < 0.001). Conclusion: Hesitancy toward and refusal of PI were observed among previously unvaccinated adults with Category III rabies exposure, yet initial hesitation or refusal is not irreversible. Early protection gap awareness was positively associated with PI choice, whereas cost-related concern was negatively associated. Clear explanation of protection timing and attention to cost-related barriers may support informed PI treatment decisions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Rabies remains a fatal yet vaccine-preventable zoonosis, with Kenya committed to the global "Zero by 30" elimination target. This study aimed to investigate whether reported vaccination coverage translates into actual humoral immunity and examine community knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) that underpin rabies control efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An across-sectional study was conducted between August 2024 and September 2025 across Kitui County (n = 322 households) and Nairobi (n = 276 households), comprising 598 household surveys administered via Kobo Collect. Canine serum samples (n = 91) from Kitui were analyzed to measure rabies virus-neutralizing antibodies (RVNA).
analysis.methods: The study used a validated competitive ELISA (Platelia® Rabies II) to measure rabies virus-neutralizing antibodies (RVNA) against the WHO/WOAH protective threshold of ≥ 0.5 IU/ml. analysis.main_results: General community awareness of rabies was high at 92.1%, with rural Kitui residents exhibiting significantly greater awareness (98.4%) than urban Nairobi residents (84.8%; p < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights a vaccination paradox where high reported vaccination coverage does not necessarily correlate with actual seroprotection, suggesting a need for improved biological monitoring of immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of biological seroprotection as a more accurate metric for rabies control than administrative vaccination coverage, with implications for surveillance and intervention strategies in Kenya.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported vaccination data and a relatively small sample size of canine serum samples. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between reported vaccination coverage and actual seroprotection against rabies in rural and urban Kenya. It highlights a vaccination paradox where high reported coverage does not equate to sufficient biological immunity. The research underscores the importance of biological monitoring over administrative data for effective rabies control. The study's findings suggest that community knowledge and attitudes play a critical role in rabies prevention. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and a limited sample size of canine serum samples may affect the strength of its conclusions. The results have implications for improving surveillance and intervention strategies in Kenya.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用经过验证的竞争性 ELISA (Platelia® 狂犬病 II) 来测量针对 WHO/WOAH ≥ 0.5 IU/ml 保护阈值的 狂犬病病毒 中和抗体 (RVNA)。多变量逻辑回归确定了 狂犬病 意识、寻求健康行为和血清阳性的独立预测因子。
elements_zh.main_results: 狂犬病 在社区中的总体认知度较高,为 92.1%,其中肯尼亚基图伊农村地区居民的认知度显著高于内罗毕城市居民(98.4% vs 84.8%;p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究揭示了 疫苗接种 的悖论现象:高报告的 疫苗接种 覆盖率并不一定与实际的血清保护水平相关,提示需加强免疫力的生物学监测。

papers.title: Design and Assembly of Combinatorial DNA Barcodes for Probe-based Genomics Applications
papers.abstract: Probe-based genomics technologies are extending molecular analysis into intact tissues and fixed cells, yet strategies to decode complex experimental conditions encoded in cellular RNA remain limited. Here we present a modular framework that integrates custom software tools with purpose-built cloning reagents to design, assemble, validate, and deploy combinatorial DNA barcodes. Combinatorial barcodes comprise spatially adjacent collections of known sequences, enabling millions of unique molecules to be efficiently distinguished using a limited set of probes. Our software tools integrate with optimized assembly plasmids and whole plasmid long-read sequencing for high-fidelity construction and structural validation of diverse combinatorial barcode architectures. Assembled barcode libraries are flexibly transferred into user-modified expression vectors to support diverse downstream experimental applications. We showcase the versatility of this framework by assembling two structurally distinct combinatorial barcode libraries, each containing millions of unique sequences. Following rabies virus-based delivery to the mouse brain, we validate in vivo decoding of a combinatorial barcode architecture capable of distinguishing ~16.3 million expressed RNAs through probe-based in situ sequencing. Our framework for flexible and accurate combinatorial barcode construction fills a technically demanding niche delivering cost-effective molecular reagents for multiplexed experimentation on current and evolving probe-based genomics platforms.

papers.title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals metabolic reprogramming and key metabolites in adherent and suspension Vero cells
papers.abstract: Introduction Vero cells are the primary host for industrial vaccine production, and high-density suspension culture is the predominant manufacturing approach. However, this method faces major challenges, including low shear tolerance, difficulty adapting to serum-free conditions, metabolic imbalance, prolonged acclimation periods, and batch-to-batch variability. Furthermore, the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying suspension adaptation remain poorly understood. Methods We established serum-free suspension adaptation of adherent Vero cells using reduction serum levels strategy. Biological characteristics of suspension-adapted cells were analyzed through morphological observation, cell viability assays, and karyotyping. A recombinant rabies vesicular stomatitis virus infection model was used to assess viral susceptibility and replication capacity. Untargeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry metabolomics was then utilized to systematically characterize intracellular metabolic profiles of Vero cells cultured under adherent and suspension conditions. Differential metabolites were identified, and key regulatory pathways were evaluated to elucidate the metabolic mechanisms of suspension adaptation and identify potential optimization targets. Results Suspension-adapted Vero cells exhibited uniform morphology, stable genetic characteristics, and robust proliferative capacity, without evidence of degeneration or mutation. Viral sensitivity assays demonstrated efficient viral adsorption and replication, yielding stable viral titers and confirming suitability for vaccine production. Metabolomic analysis identified 119 metabolites (32 upregulated, 47 downregulated, and 40 unchanged), with significant enrichment in alanine/aspartate/glutamate metabolism, glycine/serine/threonine metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Suspension cells displayed Warburg-like metabolic features, including enhanced glycolysis, increased lactate accumulation, and pronounced upregulation of succinate and malate. L-serine and ethanolamine phosphate were strongly upregulated, whereas polyunsaturated fatty acids were significantly reduced. Suspension adaptation involved coordinated remodeling of energy, amino acid, nucleotide, and lipid metabolism; enhancing shear tolerance through membrane lipid remodeling; improving antioxidant capacity via serine metabolism; and supporting high-density proliferation through glycolytic reprogramming. Discussion This study established a serum-free suspension adaptation system for Vero cells with stable phenotypic characteristics and high viral susceptibility while elucidating metabolic regulatory mechanisms that underlie suspension adaptation. The findings provide metabolic targets and a theoretical foundation for rational medium design, targeted supplementation strategies, and development of genetically engineered cell lines with enhanced shear resistance.

papers.title_zh: 非靶向代谢组学揭示贴壁和悬浮 Vero 细胞中的代谢重编程和关键代谢物
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Vero cells are the primary host for industrial vaccine production, and high-density suspension culture is the predominant manufacturing approach. However, this method faces major challenges, including low shear tolerance, difficulty adapting to serum-free conditions, metabolic imbalance, prolonged acclimation periods, and batch-to-batch variability. Furthermore, the metabolic reprogramming mechanisms underlying suspension adaptation remain poorly understood. Methods We established serum-free suspension adaptation of adherent Vero cells using reduction serum levels strategy. Biological characteristics of suspension-adapted cells were analyzed through morphological observation, cell viability assays, and karyotyping. A recombinant rabies vesicular stomatitis virus infection model was used to assess viral susceptibility and replication capacity. Untargeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry metabolomics was then utilized to systematically characterize intracellular metabolic profiles of Vero cells cultured under adherent and suspension conditions. Differential metabolites were identified, and key regulatory pathways were evaluated to elucidate the metabolic mechanisms of suspension adaptation and identify potential optimization targets. Results Suspension-adapted Vero cells exhibited uniform morphology, stable genetic characteristics, and robust proliferative capacity, without evidence of degeneration or mutation. Viral sensitivity assays demonstrated efficient viral adsorption and replication, yielding stable viral titers and confirming suitability for vaccine production. Metabolomic analysis identified 119 metabolites (32 upregulated, 47 downregulated, and 40 unchanged), with significant enrichment in alanine/aspartate/glutamate metabolism, glycine/serine/threonine metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Suspension cells displayed Warburg-like metabolic features, including enhanced glycolysis, increased lactate accumulation, and pronounced upregulation of succinate and malate. L-serine and ethanolamine phosphate were strongly upregulated, whereas polyunsaturated fatty acids were significantly reduced. Suspension adaptation involved coordinated remodeling of energy, amino acid, nucleotide, and lipid metabolism; enhancing shear tolerance through membrane lipid remodeling; improving antioxidant capacity via serine metabolism; and supporting high-density proliferation through glycolytic reprogramming. Discussion This study established a serum-free suspension adaptation system for Vero cells with stable phenotypic characteristics and high viral susceptibility while elucidating metabolic regulatory mechanisms that underlie suspension adaptation. The findings provide metabolic targets and a theoretical foundation for rational medium design, targeted supplementation strategies, and development of genetically engineered cell lines with enhanced shear resistance.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言 Vero细胞是工业化疫苗生产的主要宿主,高密度悬浮培养是主流制造工艺。然而,该方法面临多重挑战,包括低剪切耐受性、难以适应无血清条件、代谢失衡、长期驯化周期及批次间差异。此外,悬浮适应背后的代谢重编程机制尚不清楚。方法 本研究通过逐步降低血清水平策略,建立了贴壁Vero细胞的无血清悬浮适应系统。通过形态观察、细胞活力检测及核型分析,对悬浮适应细胞的生物学特性进行表征。利用重组狂犬病水泡性口炎病毒感染模型,评估病毒易感性及复制能力。随后采用非靶向液相色谱-串联质谱代谢组学,系统解析贴壁与悬浮培养条件下Vero细胞的细胞内代谢谱。识别差异代谢物,并评估关键调控通路,以阐明悬浮适应的代谢机制并挖掘潜在优化靶点。结果 悬浮适应Vero细胞形态均一、遗传特性稳定、增殖能力强,未见退化或突变现象。病毒敏感性检测显示其对病毒的吸附与复制效率高,稳定产毒且适于疫苗生产。代谢组学分析共鉴定出119个代谢物(32个上调、47个下调、40个无显著变化),显著富集于丙氨酸/天冬氨酸/谷氨酸代谢、甘氨酸/丝氨酸/苏氨酸代谢及三羧酸循环。悬浮细胞呈现Warburg样代谢特征,包括增强的糖酵解、乳酸积累增加及琥珀酸与苹果酸的显著上调。L-丝氨酸与乙醇胺磷酸强烈上调,而多不饱和脂肪酸显著下调。悬浮适应涉及能量、氨基酸、核苷酸及脂质代谢的协同重塑;通过膜脂质重塑增强剪切耐受;通过丝氨酸代谢提升抗氧化能力;并通过糖酵解重编程支持高密度增殖。讨论 本研究建立了无血清悬浮适应Vero细胞系统,其表型特征稳定且病毒易感性高,同时阐明了悬浮适应的代谢调控机制。研究结果为合理培养基设计、靶向营养补充策略及构建高剪切抗性工程细胞株提供了代谢靶点与理论基础。

news.content_title: Rabies: Public health impacts, vaccination, and exposure
news.content: Clinical Rabies: Public health impacts, vaccination, and exposure Rabies cases in companion animals and human exposures continue to make news in the United States. While veterinary professionals are well aware of the risks posed by this deadly virus, challenges such as vaccine hesitancy, variations in laws by municipality, and a lack of awareness of the seriousness of this disease contribute to the continued spread of the disease both in the U.S. and around the world. Veterinary professionals can hone their expertise and learn how to collaborate with human healthcare professionals and other public health officials to reduce the risk in their communities. Advertisement A recent news story out of Florida described a feral cat, who was later determined to be rabid, who bit at least five people and a puppy before being found dead underneath a home. After an investigation was conducted, one of the local residents who routinely fed this cat and other feral cats was cited for not having vaccinated the cats. This series of events reignited debates over responsibility to vaccinate, rabies surveillance, and other public health initiatives to protect humans and animals from the threat of rabies. Stories like these also remind veterinary teams of the lack of understanding among the general public of the risks posed by rabies to both human and animal health. Advertisement In an AAHA webinar entitled Rabies Compliance Made Clear: Protecting Pets, Clients, and Clinics, Richard Ford, DVM, MS, Dip. ACVIM and (Hon) ACVPM, discussed the state of rabies in the U.S. and around the world, important facts about vaccination, and what veterinary teams need to know about immunity and exposure. He said that when it comes to rabies, all veterinary professionals need to be experts. We caught up with him after his webinar to find out what he thinks veterinary professionals need to know the most about rabies. Human rabies impacts in the U.S. and worldwide According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), at least 70,000 people die worldwide from rabies. Forty percent of human rabies cases are in children under the age of 15, and 99% of human rabies deaths are the result of bites from rabid dogs. Ford explained that these numbers have increased since the COVID-19 pandemic for a variety of reasons, including increased vaccine hesitancy that resulted in fewer pets getting vaccinated, the breakdown of some rabies control programs that provided surveillance, and an increase in the number of stray and abandoned dogs in areas around the world. Additionally, access to healthcare for individuals bitten by a potentially rabid animal was more limited during the pandemic. In the U.S., human rabies cases are much lower than in other countries, with a total of 17 cases documented by the CDC from 2015 to 2024. Also, unlike other parts of the world, the most common rabies vectors are not dogs. Ford said that wildlife such as bats, racoons, and foxes are 10 times more likely to be infected with rabies than domestic species. And even among domestic species, cats are four times more likely to be infected with rabies than dogs are. For this reason, the top reason for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis in the U.S. is exposure to a potentially rabid cat. Even with the much lower numbers of human cases in the U.S., each case of this uniformly fatal and preventable disease is taken very seriously. 2025 AAHA One Health guidelines: Navigating Cross-Disciplinary Partnerships You know all about preventing and treating zoonotic disease, but how comfortable are you when it comes to collaborating with your colleagues in human medicine on cases that require (or simply benefit from) shared reporting? AAHA’s 2025 One Health Guidelines: Navigating Cross-Disciplinary Partnerships provides key insights and expert recommendations for what to report when—and to whom—in order to make sure we’re all working toward keeping people, pets, and the planet healthy. The guidelines also provide expert insights and detailed roadmaps to help veterinary professionals work seamlessly with other healthcare professionals within a One Health System. Read up on common scenarios, case studies, and more. Vaccination laws by jurisdiction While higher vaccination rates are undoubtedly a large part of the reason the U.S. has fewer human rabies cases than other parts of the world, laws regarding rabies vaccination of pets vary significantly from one state and municipality to the next. Ford explained that only 39 states require rabies vaccination for dogs, for example, and fewer require it for cats and ferrets. Even within states, some smaller municipalities have their own individual rules, so it can get confusing for pet owners. States also differ in which vaccines they allow companies to sell (the one-year or the three-year vaccine, for example) and who is allowed to administer the vaccine to pets. To complicate matters more, states also have varying definitions of what constitutes a “currently vaccinated” pet. Ford said most states define it as 28 days after initial vaccination and immediately after a booster, but not all states agree. Ford stressed the importance of knowing the local laws regarding rabies vaccination and following labeled indications. “It must be administered by an authorized person at the appropriate age, dose, and interval,” he said. Not doing so can lead to loss or restriction of a veterinarian’s license. Ford said that the most common rabies vaccine-related reason for action against a veterinarian’s license is giving half doses of the rabies vaccine. “Give the entire dose,” he said. Are you Rabies Aware? Wondering what your state’s laws are on rabies vaccination, quarantine after exposure, and even whether you can legally exempt a pet from vaccination requirements for medical reasons? The Rabies Aware website was created to answer all these questions and more. For U.S. state, the answers to 30 different questions about which species require vaccination, how the state defines “currently vaccinated”, and who in the state has the authority to determine exposure, among other important topics. Vaccines, immunity, and titers Ford explained why pets only need one rabies vaccine during their initial vaccination period. Other vaccines like the canine distemper vaccine or the feline leukemia vaccine require at least two doses because pets need an initial priming dose followed by at least one immunizing dose within six weeks of the first vaccine. The primary rabies vaccine given to pet still acts as the priming dose, but exposure to a rabid animal is considered to be the immunizing dose. Ford said this works because the priming dose is sustained and because the pet is considered to be immunized two weeks after exposure to a rabid animal, which is less time than the months typically needed for the virus to travel from a bite wound to the central nervous system where it causes clinical disease. In cases where there is no rabies exposure, Ford said the priming effect from the first vaccine is sustained. When the first booster is given a year later, he said antibody levels go “sky high.” But, Ford said, the presence of antibodies must be interpreted carefully. Rabies titers are currently only used for export to rabies-free areas of the world. Legally, he explained, a positive titer indicates that a pet has been vaccinated. However, a positive titer cannot be used as an indicator of immunity or protection under U.S. law, Ford said, and it does not obviate the need for a booster vaccine. Additionally, Ford said the timing of titers in relation to vaccination is very important. “If you are doing an antibody test for travel, the young cat or dog with one rabies vaccine will likely fail the test,” he said, because they have not yet had their immunizing dose of the vaccine. This is why it’s so important to draw blood for a rabies titer after a patient has had their second rabies vaccine. Ford recommends drawing the sample 3–4 weeks after the second vaccine to allow for antibodies to form prior to testing. Your trusted resources: AAHA Vaccination Guidelines and Certificate Course The 2022 AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines – AAHA, which were updated in 2024, are a helpful resource to have on hand when making vaccine recommendations to clients. While the guidelines are designed primarily for veterinary professionals, they also include information on client education. And the entire veterinary team can learn more about the vaccine guidelines (as well as how to have productive client conversations) by taking the AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines Certificate Course. To make sure you’ve got all the information you need to discuss core (and non-core) vaccines with your clients, be sure to bookmark the 2022 AAHA Canine (updated in 2024) and 2020 AAHA/AAFP Feline Vaccination Guidelines. Human and animal rabies exposure Just as with vaccination requirements, definitions of rabies exposure differ by municipality and circumstance. What constitutes an exposure, for example? Is it a bite from an animal known to be rabid? What about a scratch? What if we aren’t sure if the animal has rabies? Could just being in close proximity to certain animals be considered exposure? Ford said the answers to these questions can vary based on the types of animals involved, their vaccination and exposure history, and the types of contact or possible contact. He made one point clear, however: because of the public health risk, public health officials are the ones who decide what constitutes an exposure in any given case. When the possible exposure is between two animals, that public health official may be the state public health veterinarian, often in coordination with the treating veterinarian. In cases of possible human exposure, this will likely involve physicians or other human public health officials. Veterinary teams serve an important role in taking detailed histories and carefully documenting any known vaccinations for animals involved in possible rabies exposures. They can then use this information in their consultations with public health veterinarians to determine if an exposure is likely to have occurred and take appropriate next steps. Human healthcare professionals serve the same role for potential human exposures; however, an article in the American Journal of Infection Control identified challenges in risk determination among human healthcare professionals in the U.S. that can sometimes delay diagnosis and treatment. These challenges include the rarity of human rabies cases in the U.S., making it less of top of mind as a differential diagnosis, and the relatively long incubation period in between a possible exposure and the appearance of any symptoms of disease, which can make it less likely that a potential exposure would be mentioned or considered as part of a patient’s medical history. A separate study in the Archives of Academic Emergency Medicine conducted in Iran documented “significant shortcomings among healthcare professionals” in knowledge of potential rabies vector species, routes of transmission, and post-exposure management of patients. Although veterinary and human healthcare professionals typically have a high level of understanding of rabies pathophysiology, prevention, and post-exposure management, there is great value in these two groups working together design preventive strategies, identify cases where intervention is needed, and educate the general public as to the risks of this deadly disease. Stories like these also remind veterinary teams of the lack of understanding among the general public of the risks posed by rabies to both human and animal health. Advertisement In an AAHA webinar entitled Rabies Compliance Made Clear: Protecting Pets, Clients, and Clinics, Richard Ford, DVM, MS, Dip. ACVIM and (Hon) ACVPM, discussed the state of rabies in the U.S. and around the world, important facts about vaccination, and what veterinary teams need to know about immunity and exposure. He said that when it comes to rabies, all veterinary professionals need to be experts. We caught up with him after his webinar to find out what he thinks veterinary professionals need to know the most about rabies. Human rabies impacts in the U.S. and worldwide According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), at least 70,000 people die worldwide from rabies. Forty percent of human rabies cases are in children under the age of 15, and 99% of human rabies deaths are the result of bites from rabid dogs. Ford explained that these numbers have increased since the COVID-19 pandemic for a variety of reasons, including increased vaccine hesitancy that resulted in fewer pets getting vaccinated, the breakdown of some rabies control programs that provided surveillance, and an increase in the number of stray and abandoned dogs in areas around the world. Additionally, access to healthcare for individuals bitten by a potentially rabid animal was more limited during the pandemic. In the U.S., human rabies cases are much lower than in other countries, with a total of 17 cases documented by the CDC from 2015 to 2024. Also, unlike other parts of the world, the most common rabies vectors are not dogs. Ford said that wildlife such as bats, racoons, and foxes are 10 times more likely to be infected with rabies than domestic species. And even among domestic species, cats are four times more likely to be infected with rabies than dogs are. For this reason, the top reason for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis in the U.S. is exposure to a potentially rabid cat. Even with the much lower numbers of human cases in the U.S., each case of this uniformly fatal and preventable disease is taken very seriously. 2025 AAHA One Health guidelines: Navigating Cross-Disciplinary Partnerships You know all about preventing and treating zoonotic disease, but how comfortable are you when it comes to collaborating with your colleagues in human medicine on cases that require (or simply benefit from) shared reporting? AAHA’s 2025 One Health Guidelines: Navigating Cross-Disciplinary Partnerships provides key insights and expert recommendations for what to report when—and to whom—in order to make sure we’re all working toward keeping people, pets, and the planet healthy. The guidelines also provide expert insights and detailed roadmaps to help veterinary professionals work seamlessly with other healthcare professionals within a One Health System. Read up on common scenarios, case studies, and more. Vaccination laws by jurisdiction While higher vaccination rates are undoubtedly a large part of the reason the U.S. has fewer human rabies cases than other parts of the world, laws regarding rabies vaccination of pets vary significantly from one state and municipality to the next. Ford explained that only 39 states require rabies vaccination for dogs, for example, and fewer require it for cats and ferrets. Even within states, some smaller municipalities have their own individual rules, so it can get confusing for pet owners. States also differ in which vaccines they allow companies to sell (the one-year or the three-year vaccine, for example) and who is allowed to administer the vaccine to pets. To complicate matters more, states also have varying definitions of what constitutes a “currently vaccinated” pet. Ford said most states define it as 28 days after initial vaccination and immediately after a booster, but not all states agree. Ford stressed the importance of knowing the local laws regarding rabies vaccination and following labeled indications. “It must be administered by an authorized person at the appropriate age, dose, and interval,” he said. Not doing so can lead to loss or restriction of a veterinarian’s license. Ford said that the most common rabies vaccine-related reason for action against a veterinarian’s license is giving half doses of the rabies vaccine. “Give the entire dose,” he said. Are you Rabies Aware? Wondering what your state’s laws are on rabies vaccination, quarantine after exposure, and even whether you can legally exempt a pet from vaccination requirements for medical reasons? The Rabies Aware website was created to answer all these questions and more. For U.S. state, the answers to 30 different questions about which species require vaccination, how the state defines “currently vaccinated”, and who in the state has the authority to determine exposure, among other important topics. Vaccines, immunity, and titers Ford explained why pets only need one rabies vaccine during their initial vaccination period. Other vaccines like the canine distemper vaccine or the feline leukemia vaccine require at least two doses because pets need an initial priming dose followed by at least one immunizing dose within six weeks of the first vaccine. The primary rabies vaccine given to pet still acts as the priming dose, but exposure to a rabid animal is considered to be the immunizing dose. Ford said this works because the priming dose is sustained and because the pet is considered to be immunized two weeks after exposure to a rabid animal, which is less time than the months typically needed for the virus to travel from a bite wound to the central nervous system where it causes clinical disease. In cases where there is no rabies exposure, Ford said the priming effect from the first vaccine is sustained. When the first booster is given a year later, he said antibody levels go “sky high.” But, Ford said, the presence of antibodies must be interpreted carefully. Rabies titers are currently only used for export to rabies-free areas of the world. Legally, he explained, a positive titer indicates that a pet has been vaccinated. However, a positive titer cannot be used as an indicator of immunity or protection under U.S. law, Ford said, and it does not obviate the need for a booster vaccine. Additionally, Ford said the timing of titers in relation to vaccination is very important. “If you are doing an antibody test for travel, the young cat or dog with one rabies vaccine will likely fail the test,” he said, because they have not yet had their immunizing dose of the vaccine. This is why it’s so important to draw blood for a rabies titer after a patient has had their second rabies vaccine. Ford recommends drawing the sample 3–4 weeks after the second vaccine to allow for antibodies to form prior to testing. Your trusted resources: AAHA Vaccination Guidelines and Certificate Course The 2022 AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines – AAHA, which were updated in 2024, are a helpful resource to have on hand when making vaccine recommendations to clients. While the guidelines are designed primarily for veterinary professionals, they also include information on client education. And the entire veterinary team can learn more about the vaccine guidelines (as well as how to have productive client conversations) by taking the AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines Certificate Course. To make sure you’ve got all the information you need to discuss core (and non-core) vaccines with your clients, be sure to bookmark the 2022 AAHA Canine (updated in 2024) and 2020 AAHA/AAFP Feline Vaccination Guidelines. Human and animal rabies exposure Just as with vaccination requirements, definitions of rabies exposure differ by municipality and circumstance. What constitutes an exposure, for example? Is it a bite from an animal known to be rabid? What about a scratch? What if we aren’t sure if the animal has rabies? Could just being in close proximity to certain animals be considered exposure? Ford said the answers to these questions can vary based on the types of animals involved, their vaccination and exposure history, and the types of contact or possible contact. He made one point clear, however: because of the public health risk, public health officials are the ones who decide what constitutes an exposure in any given case. When the possible exposure is between two animals, that public health official may be the state public health veterinarian, often in coordination with the treating veterinarian. In cases of possible human exposure, this will likely involve physicians or other human public health officials. Veterinary teams serve an important role in taking detailed histories and carefully documenting any known vaccinations for animals involved in possible rabies exposures. They can then use this information in their consultations with public health veterinarians to determine if an exposure is likely to have occurred and take appropriate next steps. Human healthcare professionals serve the same role for potential human exposures; however, an article in the American Journal of Infection Control identified challenges in risk determination among human healthcare professionals in the U.S. that can sometimes delay diagnosis and treatment. These challenges include the rarity of human rabies cases in the U.S., making it less of top of mind as a differential diagnosis, and the relatively long incubation period in between a possible exposure and the appearance of any symptoms of disease, which can make it less likely that a potential exposure would be mentioned or considered as part of a patient’s medical history. A separate study in the Archives of Academic Emergency Medicine conducted in Iran documented “significant shortcomings among healthcare professionals” in knowledge of potential rabies vector species, routes of transmission, and post-exposure management of patients. Although veterinary and human healthcare professionals typically have a high level of understanding of rabies pathophysiology, prevention, and post-exposure management, there is great value in these two groups working together design preventive strategies, identify cases where intervention is needed, and educate the general public as to the risks of this deadly disease. news.content_zh: 美国动物医院协会(AAHA)于2026年8月24日发布指导意见,概述了狂犬病(狂犬病)持续的公共卫生负担:全球每年至少70,000人死亡,其中40%为15岁以下儿童,99%的死亡由犬类咬伤导致。在美国,2015年至2024年间共记录17例人类病例;野生动物(如蝙蝠、浣熊和狐狸)携带狂犬病(狂犬病病毒)的风险是家养动物的10倍,而猫携带该病毒的风险是犬的4倍。在美国,暴露后预防(狂犬病暴露后预防)最常由疑似狂犬病的猫接触引发。文章强调了各司法管辖区在狂犬病(狂犬病)疫苗接种(预防与控制)法律上的差异:仅39个州强制要求犬类疫苗接种(疫苗接种),而对猫和雪貂的要求更少。此外,COVID-19疫情加剧了挑战,包括疫苗(疫苗接种)犹豫、监测(医疗服务)减少及医疗资源紧张。AAHA于2025年发布的《一体化健康》指南呼吁加强兽医与人医的协作,以强化预防与控制。
